questions.question: First apply filter_by_category(field=Product type, values=[haircare, cosmetics]). Describe how manufacturing lead time, cost, volume, and defect signals spread for that skincare subset—are the lines bundled or all over the place?

answer.value: Skincare polylines do not collapse to a single sweet spot: normalized lead times and costs sweep from near-zero up to the top of each axis, so you see both budget fast-turn items and slow, expensive runs. Production volume and defect rate add more spread—some SKUs hug high-volume / low-defect bundles, others drift toward low-volume tails. Overall it feels like several manufacturing strategies coexisting rather than one dominant cluster.

key_insights: Lead time and manufacturing cost show wide dispersion even after restricting to skincare.
Volume and defect axes contribute crossing lines, hinting at multiple operating models within the same product family.

reasoning.reasoning: Removes non-skincare categories so parallel coordinates reflect one product class.
